title: plan-parallel recommends a wave plan for running slices in parallel
findings_note: owner 2026-10-18: recommend a parallel implementation path, like `next` for parallel work; the v1.14 and v1.15 relay runs planned their waves by hand from each slice's Files and dependencies
boundary: **Not in this slice:** starting or claiming items, spawning relays, changing `next --batch --disjoint`, or predicting conflicts beyond the Files sections' paths.

sections.heading: Why
sections.body: `next --batch K --disjoint` answers what can run side by side right now. A parallel run needs the whole path: what runs first, what becomes ready and disjoint once that lands, and why each slice sits where it does. The v1.15 run built that table by hand (six relays in wave 1, six in wave 2, ordered by dependency and shared files). `slicer plan-parallel` computes it from state that slicer already has.

sections.heading: Files
sections.body:
- `src/slicer/ops.py`: `plan_parallel(state, width, *, tree, size, max_attempts, flags, no_flags)`. It reuses `_ranked_pool`, `graph.pending`, `item_paths` and `counted_paths` the way `next_batch` does, and returns a dataclass with `to_dict` in a fixed key order.
- `src/slicer/cli.py`: the `plan-parallel` parser and command (text and `--json`, `--lean`).
- `tests/test_plan_parallel.py`.
- `docs/commands.md` (row), `docs/agents.md` (JSON contract), `CHANGELOG.md` under Added.

sections.heading: Implement
sections.body:
1. Write the tests; watch them go red.
2. Waves. Wave 0 lists items already started (in flight); their paths count as taken for wave 1. Each wave then fills greedily in `next` rank order, up to `--width N` (default 4), with items that are:
   - not yet placed;
   - with every pending dependency done or in an earlier wave;
   - with counted paths disjoint from the paths taken in this wave.
   After a wave, its paths are released and the next wave starts. Stop when no item can be placed.
3. A reason for each placement after wave 1: the dependency it waits on (`after: ID`) or the item whose paths it shares (`shares: ID path`). Items with no paths in their files section go under `unplaced` with reason `no_files`, like `unknown_files`; held, unspecified and capped items are reported the way `next` reports them.
4. Text output: one block per wave (`wave N`, then `ID  short title  reason`). JSON: `{width, waves: [{wave, items: [{id, title, reason}]}], in_flight, unplaced, blocked}`. No lock, no write.
5. It needs `files_section` the way `--disjoint` does: without it, refuse with the same code.
6. Docs, CHANGELOG; mutation-check.

sections.heading: Check
sections.body:
- `python3.12 tests/affected.py --run`, then the full suite. `slicer check` passes.
- On this repo, `slicer plan-parallel --width 4` places the open v1.16 items, and each later-wave item names its reason.

sections.body: One commit on the slice branch; the owner lands it.
